headline:
School life,
one question away.
summary: Term Time reads the school's website, calendar, newsletters and emails, plus whatever turns up in the parents' WhatsApp group, and answers questions about any of it in plain English.

statement.label: Why I built it
statement.text: A primary school sends a lot: newsletters, letters, calendar changes, PDFs and class emails. The one detail you need is always in the one you didn't read.

points.title: The website
points.text: Term dates, clubs and lunch menus, often as PDFs, and sometimes a year out of date.

points.title: The calendar
points.text: Trips and assemblies, each one a single line with no detail.

points.title: The inbox
points.text: The weekly newsletter, letters home, and what to bring on the day.

points.title: The WhatsApp group
points.text: Open evenings, spelling lists and photos of the letter in the book bag.

exampleQuestions: When do we go back after half term?
When is the next school trip?
Was there a newsletter last week?
What are this week's Year 3 spellings?
When are the secondary school open evenings?

highlights.title: Term dates and holidays
highlights.text: Half terms, INSET days and the first day back, read from the school's own calendar feed rather than a page that can go stale.
highlights.imageAlt: Term Time answering "When is half term?" with the dates and a link to the school calendar.

highlights.title: Trips and events, by year group
highlights.text: Pick your children's year groups and answers lead with their trips, letters and spelling lists.
highlights.imageAlt: Term Time with Year 6 selected, answering a question about the next school trip.

highlights.title: Fed from the WhatsApp group too
highlights.text: Paste a message or photograph a letter in the admin console. Term Time pulls out the dates and follows any links.
highlights.imageAlt: The admin console's Paste a note screen, with a message from a parents' group ready to save.

demo.title: A narrated walkthrough
demo.summary: Recorded in the browser with Playwright and narrated with Google's text-to-speech, in the same Australian voice as this site's blog narration.
